theory.intro: Mass tells us how heavy something is. We choose a unit and a measuring device to suit the size of the object.
facts: **Grams ($\text{g}$)** suit light objects (an apple, a pencil).
**Kilograms ($\text{kg}$)** suit everyday objects (a bag of flour, a person).
**Tonnes ($\text{t}$)** suit very heavy objects (a car, a truck, an elephant).
Kitchen scales suit ingredient masses; bathroom scales suit people; weighbridges suit heavy loads. Check capacity and how fine a reading is needed.
steps: Think about the object and whether its stated mass is sensible. Choose grams for light objects, kilograms for everyday masses or tonnes for very heavy loads.
Choose a device suited to the object. Its maximum capacity must be at least the mass being measured; small masses may need a finer reading.
State the unit and device requested, and explain why they suit the object. If a stated unit is unreasonable, correct it without changing a sensible number.

workedExamples.question_text:
Choose a sensible mass unit for each.
(a) A rubber eraser
(b) A school bag
(c) A loaded cement truck
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) An eraser is light. Use grams ($\text{g}$).
(b) A school bag has a mass of a few kilograms. Use kilograms ($\text{kg}$).
(c) A loaded truck is very heavy, with a mass of thousands of kilograms. Use tonnes ($\text{t}$).

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Choose between scales that read to the nearest $10\text{ g}$ and precision scales to measure a $3\text{ g}$ seed sample.
(b) A crate has a mass of about $31\text{ kg}$. Choose between bench scales with a maximum capacity of $8\text{ kg}$ and platform scales with a maximum capacity of $120\text{ kg}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use precision scales reading grams. A reading to the nearest $10\text{ g}$ is too coarse for a $3\text{ g}$ sample.
(b) $31\text{ kg}>8\text{ kg}$, so the crate is too heavy for the bench scales.
$31\text{ kg}<120\text{ kg}$, so use the platform scales reading kilograms.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A guitar label gives its mass as $5.8\text{ g}$. Correct the likely unit error.
(b) Can scales with a maximum capacity of $40\text{ kg}$ measure a box expected to have a mass of $87\text{ kg}$? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $5.8\text{ g}$ is far too light for a guitar. The sensible mass is $5.8\text{ kg}$.
(b) $87\text{ kg}>40\text{ kg}$. No; the box exceeds the scales' maximum capacity. Use a higher-capacity device.

foundation.question_text: Choose the most appropriate unit for the mass of a strawberry: $\text{g}$, $\text{kg}$ or $\text{t}$.
foundation.solution_text:
A strawberry is light, so grams are appropriate.
$\text{Unit}=\text{g}$

foundation.question_text: Choose the most appropriate unit for the mass of a primary school student: $\text{g}$, $\text{kg}$ or $\text{t}$.
foundation.solution_text:
A person's mass is usually measured in kilograms.
$\text{Unit}=\text{kg}$

foundation.question_text: Choose the most appropriate unit for the mass of a loaded shipping container: $\text{g}$, $\text{kg}$ or $\text{t}$.
foundation.solution_text:
A loaded shipping container is very heavy, so tonnes are appropriate.
$\text{Unit}=\text{t}$

foundation.question_text: Which device is most suitable for measuring $180\text{ g}$ of flour: kitchen scales, bathroom scales or a weighbridge?
foundation.solution_text:
Kitchen scales are designed to measure ingredient masses in grams.
The suitable device is **kitchen scales**.

foundation.question_text: Which device is most suitable for measuring the mass of a suitcase: kitchen scales, luggage scales or a weighbridge?
foundation.solution_text:
A suitcase has a mass of several kilograms, within the range of luggage scales.
The suitable device is **luggage scales**.

foundation.question_text: Which device is most suitable for measuring the mass of a delivery truck: bathroom scales, parcel scales or a weighbridge?
foundation.solution_text:
A truck has a mass of thousands of kilograms, so it needs a weighbridge.
The suitable device is **a weighbridge**.

development.question_text:
A bakery needs to measure the mass of one bread roll.
Choose a sensible unit and device.
development.solution_text:
A bread roll is a light object whose mass is sensibly recorded in grams.
Use **grams and kitchen scales**.

development.question_text:
A veterinarian needs to measure the mass of a large dog.
Choose a sensible unit and device.
development.solution_text:
A large dog's mass is several kilograms.
Use **kilograms and animal scales**.

development.question_text:
A recycling centre needs to record the mass of a truckload of metal.
Choose a sensible unit and device.
development.solution_text:
A truckload has a mass of thousands of kilograms.
Use **tonnes and a weighbridge**.

development.question_text:
A jeweller wants to measure a silver ring accurately.
Would bathroom scales or precision scales be more appropriate, and which unit should be used?
development.solution_text:
A ring is light and needs a fine reading.
Use **precision scales and grams**.

development.question_text:
A farmer estimates that a cow has a mass of $620$.
What unit makes this estimate sensible?
development.solution_text:
A cow's mass is hundreds of kilograms, not grams or tonnes.
The sensible unit is $\text{kg}$.

development.question_text:
A road sign limits vehicles to a mass of $4.5$.
What unit makes this limit sensible?
development.solution_text:
A vehicle limit of $4.5$ is sensibly measured in tonnes.
The sensible unit is $\text{t}$.

mastery.question_text:
A science class has precision scales, platform scales and a weighbridge.
It must measure a $2\text{ g}$ seed sample and a $28\text{ kg}$ box.
Choose the most appropriate available device and unit for each.
mastery.solution_text:
The seed sample needs precision scales reading grams.
The box needs platform scales reading kilograms.
Use **precision scales in grams** and **platform scales in kilograms**.

mastery.question_text:
A warehouse scale has a maximum capacity of $150\text{ kg}$.
Can it be used to measure a pallet expected to have a mass of about $1\text{ t}$?
Explain.
mastery.solution_text:
$1\text{ t}$ is much more than $150\text{ kg}$.
The pallet is outside the scale's range, so **a higher-capacity device is needed**.

mastery.question_text:
A label says a bicycle has a mass of $14\text{ g}$.
Identify the likely error and give a sensible unit.
mastery.solution_text:
$14\text{ g}$ is far too light for a bicycle.
The number is sensible in kilograms, so the label should read $14\text{ kg}$.
